spec_match.rationale: Demonstrates the precise semantic the keywords name — flow-relative vs logical start under placement reversal — with measured geometry, and presents the Grid Lanes motivation without faking an unshippable masonry demo.

interactive.rationale: Direction, dir, and alignment button groups restyle a real flexbox with per-click measured offsets, plus a one-click eight-combination divergence table.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises measured divergence under row-reverse/rtl/column-reverse; the playground and table deliver it.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers rtl-with-reversal double flips, the dropped flow-* keyword path with a labelled spec-defined alias (after fixing a stale-inline-value mask found during verification), and an unexpected-no-divergence warning.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5069051687731200 and the masonry item-flow CSSWG issue 12803.

conformance.rationale: The suite's flow-relative-divergence assertion automates this page's core measurement and passes today, pinning the semantic the aliases inherit.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud fallback, no chrome-devtools-mcp): row/ltr start measured 10px; row-reverse flex-start 610px vs start 138px (the split, live); flow-start showed the DROPPED label and applied the alias to identical geometry; the table measured 0/0, 250/250, 0/250, 250/0 with both reversed rows flagged DIVERGED; zero console errors; both viewports clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts every measurement with its full state payload (direction, dir, requested vs applied value, aliased flag, offset) and the table's divergence outcome.

design_system.rationale: Tokens only; the first chip inverts background and color together; pressed states are outline-based on light backgrounds; 44px targets.

accessibility.rationale: All controls are native buttons in labelled groups with aria-pressed, physical-edge labels are decorative while the readout carries offsets as text in a polite live region, and the playground is fully keyboard-operable.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×800: controls wrap to multiple rows, zero overflow, identical measurements.

openQuestions.title: Build the Grid Lanes reversal rig when an engine ships item-flow reversal
openQuestions.detail: The feature's target case — align-content: flow-start under item-flow: track-reverse in display: grid-lanes — is not implementable in any current engine, so this portfolio demonstrates the semantic with flexbox. When Chromium ships Grid Lanes reversal (even flagged), add a measured masonry rig showing start vs flow-start diverging outside flexbox for the first time.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Understand flexbox main-axis alignment as content-first with flow-relative semantics; use gap and wrap for control rows.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The playground's explanation text distinguishes logical vs flow-relative per the guide's flexbox model, and all control rows wrap with gap tokens.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detect CSS value support graceful fallback
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: A fallback must be labelled and must clear prior state so detection stays falsifiable.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The dropped-keyword path removes the previous inline value before probing (bug caught in verification) and prints an explicit 'labelled fallback, not a simulation' line naming the alias applied.

summary: The why of flow-start, measured: 610px vs 138px for flex-start vs start in a row-reverse flexbox, a full eight-combination divergence table, and an honestly-labelled alias fallback for the unparsed keywords. Verification caught and fixed a stale-inline-value bug that could have masked the fallback. Cloud headless Chromium 141, both viewports clean.
